back: Ground (horizontal view), oblique aerial (at an angle; high oblique shows the horizon), vertical aerial (straight down, map-like).
Divide into foreground (bottom, nearest), middle ground and background (top, furthest); describe relief, vegetation, land use, settlement.
Collecting information about the Earth's surface from a distance (satellites, aircraft, drones) by recording reflected or emitted radiation.
Gamma → X-rays → ultraviolet → visible (≈400–700 nm) → infrared → microwaves → radio (short to long).
Absorbs blue and red (chlorophyll), reflects some green and strongly reflects near-infrared.
Near-infrared shown as red: healthy vegetation bright red, clear water dark, towns blue-grey.
Passive: record reflected sunlight (need daylight, clear skies). Active (radar): send microwaves, work through cloud and at night.
Visiting sample sites to check that an image interpretation matches what is really on the ground.
